messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

message.content:
The offset between Los Angeles (Pacific Time) and Berlin (Central European Time) changes with daylight‑saving transitions.  
| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|------------|
| **Standard‑time only** (both on standard time) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **+9 h** (Berlin is 9 h ahead) |
| **Los Angeles on DST, Berlin on standard** (early‑March to late‑March) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **+8 h** |
| **Both on DST** (late‑March to late‑October) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **+9 h** |
| **Berlin on DST, Los Angeles on standard** (late‑October to early‑November) | UTC‑8 | UTC+2 | **+10 h** |

So, for most of the year the difference is 9 hours, but it can be 8 hours in the first few weeks of March and 10 hours in the last weeks of October. If you need the exact offset for a specific date, let me know the date and I can calculate it for you.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?" They want the time difference. We need to provide the answer. We can compute the time difference. Los Angeles is in Pacific Time Zone (PT), which is UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 daylight saving. Berlin is Central European Time (CET) UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 daylight saving. So difference is 9 hours during standard time (Los Angeles UTC-8 vs Berlin UTC+1 => 9 hours). During daylight saving, Los Angeles UTC-7 vs Berlin UTC+2 => 9 hours as well. Actually both shift at same time? Los Angeles DST starts second Sunday in March, ends first Sunday in November. Berlin DST starts last Sunday in March, ends last Sunday in October. So there is a period where difference is 8 hours? Let's check: In early March before DST starts in Berlin but after Los Angeles DST? Actually Los Angeles DST starts earlier (second Sunday March). Berlin DST starts later (last Sunday March). So between second Sunday March and last Sunday March, Los Angeles is on DST (UTC-7) while Berlin is still on standard (UTC+1). So difference is 8 hours. After Berlin DST starts, both are on DST: Los Angeles UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2 => difference 9 hours. After Los Angeles DST ends (first Sunday November), Los Angeles goes back to UTC-8, Berlin remains on DST until last Sunday October. So between last Sunday October and first Sunday November, Berlin is on DST (UTC+2) while Los Angeles is on standard (UTC-8) => difference 10 hours. After both on standard again, difference 9 hours.

So the time difference varies between 8, 9, and 10 hours depending on date. The user didn't specify date. We can give general answer: Usually 9 hours difference, but can be 8 or 10 depending on DST. Provide explanation. No function needed.
